The idea is simple:

1) A mod can tag or "add flair" to any post or comment on their sub using any moderation action. For example: "spam" or "against the rules".

2) When a user goes to /v/<sub> then they won't see any post or comment which mods tagged as "spam" or "against the rules".

3) A user can ignore any and all mod actions site-wide by setting "ignore mod actions" in their user profile. If set, then rule #2 above is ignored wherever the user goes and they see everything. Posts and comments will still show any flair or tags that a mod added.

4) When a user goes to a sub and clicks on the "new" tab, then they see everything unfiltered including any and all posts or comments. Posts and comments here will still show any flair or tags that a mod added.

5) Within any particular post, there is a new "unfiltered comments" tab. When a user clicks on this tab, any and all comments in that post are displayed unfiltered. Comments in this post will still show any flair or tags that a mod added.

That's it. This disallows mods from deleting any content while still giving them control over their sub's default filter. IMHO mods should not be allowed to delete anything at all.

Thoughts?
Disallow deletion of any post or comment from a sub. Instead, make it a filter.

I respectfully do not like this idea.

I agree though the problem of spam has to be figured out first. I think a mechanism for removing spam and hiding it from search engine results is a given, but at the same time won't exclude content any mod intended to censor.
